previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of two kidney transplants, and recent upper extremity deep vein thrombosis was admitted for fever, chills, and cloudy urine. She had a urine culture from clinic one week prior showing Klebsiella pneumoniae that was not treated. She met SIRS criteria on presentation due to fever and was started on intravenous cefepime in the emergency department, later switched to ceftazidime. Blood cultures remained negative, and she became afebrile within 48 hours. Urine culture confirmed Klebsiella sensitive to ciprofloxacin, and she was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for a 14-day course. Renal ultrasound showed elevated resistive indices, attributed to inflammatory changes from infection rather than rejection. A chest X-ray revealed a resolving left upper lobe pneumonia, with follow-up imaging recommended. She continued all home medications, including immunosuppressants and apixaban. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics and follow up on her chest imaging.

Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Klebsiella pneumoniae [K. pneumoniae] as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
